event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Semis ripped, defensives and real assets bled; narrow tape.
The week belonged to AI hardware, with SOXX +7.43% doing the heavy lifting and dragging QQQ +3.19% higher, while every small-cap and equal-weight proxy finished red (IWM -0.75%, RSP -0.56%). What lagged was the real-asset and defensive complex — utilities, energy, gold, silver — as money rotated hard into growth. Breadth was the tell: only 26% of S&P names above their 50-day.

INDICES — QQQ +3.19%, SPY +1.27%, DIA +0.31%, IWM -0.75% ranked best to worst, with SOXX +7.43% the outlier leader. Large beat small by 3.63pp. VIX sits at 14.9, below its 20-day 15.7 — vol compressed into the rally. Biggest cross-asset move: USO -3.11% Friday, with UNG -3.64%; UUP sits +2.14% over 20 days. IWM, IJH (-4.77% 20d), IJR, and RSP all trade below their 200-day.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLK +3.52%, XLC +1.94%, XLV +1.37%, XLI +0.40%, XLB -0.38%, XLY -0.42%, XLP -0.89%, XLF -1.83%, XLRE -2.28%, XLE -3.53%, XLU -3.87%. Top industries: SOXX +7.43%, SMH +5.86%; bottom: XOP -4.78%, FCG -4.07%. Money went into XLY +$711mm (100th pctile), XLK +$147mm, XLC +$138mm; out of XLF -$2,305mm and XLV -$1,089mm. Narrow mega-cap tape.

DRIVERS — The mechanical story is semiconductors absorbing nearly all incremental flow: SOXX +$1,797mm (100th pctile) with SOXX volume at just 0.6x average, meaning the move came on light participation, not broad accumulation. Energy was the funding source — XLE -3.53% and XOP -4.78% as crude fell and EIA crude inventories built 296.9k versus a -64.1k forecast. Friday's University of Michigan sentiment final at 48.1 beat 47.6, and 1-year inflation expectations held at 4.6%, while durable goods printed 0.0% against -0.4% forecast. No Fed event occurred this week; the next FOMC is Oct 28.

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch whether SOXX can hold its +7.43% week given that only 46% of S&P names sit above their 200-day and new 60-day lows (46) outnumber highs (15) — a divergence that resolves either by broadening or by semis giving it back. SPY max pain at 770 vs. spot 769.77 and QQQ max pain at 735 vs. 745.65 sets up pinning risk into month-end. Core PCE (fc 3.40% y/y) and final Q2 GDP (fc 1.6%) land Sept 30, with Polymarket pricing a 62% chance of a 25bp hike at the October meeting — a hawkish tail the growth complex is not positioned for.
